newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: EA-Generali meets on Creditanstalt bid.
newsitem.headline: EA-Generali meets on Creditanstalt bid.

text.p: Insurer EA-Generali and its partners meet on Wednesday to decide whether to top up their offer for Austrian sell-off candidate Creditanstalt, a spokesman for EA-Generali said.
"The meeting will begin this afternoon, but I don't expect we will have a statement before Friday," he told Reuters.

EA-Generali and its partners, which include savings bank Die Erste, Germany's Commerzbank and Banca Commercialie Italiana, have offered a total of 13.8 billion schillings ($1.3 billion) for the state's 19.9 million shares in the bank and want to sell about a quarter of those on the market at a premium, most which would also go to the government.

The group is up against a rival bid by market leader Bank Austria, which has bid some 16.8 billion schillings for the entire bank stake, and an outside offer by entrepreneur Karl Wlaschek, details of which have not been released.

Finance Minister Viktor Klima, trying to steer Europe's longest-running privatisation project through increasingly treacherous political waters, has given bidders a final January 10 deadline to top up their bids and wants to decide on the buyer for Creditanstalt soon afterwards.

Bank Austria is the preferred candidate of Klima's Social Democratic Party, while EA-Generali is supported by the conservative People's Party, the Social Democrat's junior government coalition partners. The debate over the sale, now in its seventh year, has put growing strain on the government.
Klima said on Tuesday he would accept the "best and highest offer" for Creditanstalt.

Sources close to the consortium were quoted as saying last week they would be hard pressed to come up with the extra 2.8 billion schillings required to match their rival's bid, saying they had all but given up hope of getting their hands on the country's most traditional bank.
